title.narrative: Strengthening Women and Youth Participation in Peacebuilding and Civic Space in Conflict Hotspots in Leer and Rubkona

description.narrative: The prolonged civil wars in South Sudan has increased gender inequality, sexual and gender-based violence, compounded by limited education and economic opportunities for youth among others. Disruption of youth education and economic opportunities has had dramatic impact on Youth Peace and Security in a Country with a youth bulge of 51% and 70% being under the age of 30. In South Sudan – a country affected by conflict and violence, youth are commonly perceived as either perpetrators or victims. On the other hand, women make up-to 80% of the Agricultural labour in South Sudan yet have no control over resources. Few are in Governance despite allocations of 35% quota, a factor leading to increased gender inequality which undermines Women Peace and Security efforts. Pervasive negative social and cultural norms, gender-based violence, and barriers to socio-economic empowerment continue to hinder progress towards genuine gender equality and hence impacting WPS efforts. Women peace and Security and Youth Peace and Security are continually overlooked and little effort is put into engagement of youth and women in leadership and in the peace process. The “Strengthening Women and Youth participation in Peacebuilding and Civic Spaces in Conflict Hotspots” project aims to empower women and youth in Leer and Rubkona Counties of Unity State to take up active roles in the peacebuilding process.
